newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says no more oil price hikes before July.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says no more oil price hikes before July.

text.p: Taiwan state monopoly Chinese Petroleum said on Thursday it would not raise petrol prices before July 1 despite an accumulated budget deficit of T$15.896 billion.
Chinese Petroleum president Wenent Pan gave the assurance under questioning in parliament, state television reported.
Company officials confirmed Pan's statement, but declined to comment further.

Chinese Petroleum raised domestic oil prices an average nine percent on January 1 and a further 2.97 percent on April 5, saying the increases were needed to whittle down its cumulative budget deficit at a time of higher-than-expected crude costs.
Chinese Petroleum had an accumulated deficit of T$15.896 billion for the first seven months of its fiscal year, which began on July 1, officials said.
The company said it paid an average US$20.26 a barrel for crude in March, far above the US$15.26 it had budgeted for.
